label: copy-phase input 3 (recall position >= 3)
explanation: Fires almost exclusively in the copy phase when the fed-back input token is the digit 3, i.e. the model just emitted a 3 and is now outputting the original token after it. Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, or on other tokens (the few non-3 hits are tiny). It is almost silent when the 3 comes in at recall_idx 2 (the 3 was original token 1) and fires at about the same rate from recall_idx 3 on. Magnitude is larger later in the copy (low-quartile examples are at recall_idx 2-3, top examples at 5-6), and when two 3s come in a row the second is weaker than the first. The output token does not modulate it. False positives are mostly early-position 3s that stay silent.

issues: The core claims hold up. The feature never fires in the original or delimiter phases (0 active). In_tok=3 carries 100% of the activation mass; all other tokens together fire on fewer than 200 steps. The test score matches the report: P 0.984, R 0.954, F1 0.969, mass recall 0.991.

Firing rate on copy-phase 3s by recall_idx: precision is 0.945 at recall_idx 3 and about 0.9999-1.0 at recall_idx 4-8. So the false positives the predicate still has are concentrated at recall_idx 3, mostly in sequences of length L=6-9, where precision is 0.89-0.95.

'Nearly silent at recall_idx 2' needs a length qualifier. At recall_idx 2 the feature fires on 65% of copy-phase 3s when L=4 and 46% when L=3, against only 1-4% when L>=6. These firings are weak: all misses together hold 0.9% of the activation mass.

Claims I checked: 3s at recall_idx>=3 that follow another 3 are still active (precision 0.974). The 'correct==0' case is negligible (1 step). In the profile, the output token makes no difference (rates are flat across out_tok, about 0.019-0.022).
